groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats. Welcome!
M: It's my pleasure.
W: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service. However, before we talk about that, I'd like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia. What can you tell us?
M: I'm afraid I don't know much beyond what we've all seen on the news. It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy, and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on. But my career work has mostly focused around the continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I've never been involved with Winopian relations. It's for this reason that I don't know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
W: Oh, I see.
M: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our expert envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation, and I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
W: So how does one get a career in foreign relations?
M: There are many different paths one can take. All diplomats have their own story. But in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering followed by six years' service in the air force. Then I went to law school, and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic corps where I have been for 22 years.
W: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job?
M: There are so many. Being a hard worker and a good student is important. You never stop learning. In addition, a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric. Whether it is defusing attention or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: It's getting late and we're both displaying signs of weariness. I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning.
W: Oh, come on, Jeff. We are so close! Don't you think we are almost done? Let's do two more hours, please.
M: One hour, then I'm going home.
W: OK, fine. I think we are making good progress, and that with a few more amendments, we will be all done.
M: I'm sure looking forward to it. I'm so tired of this project. Don't get me wrong. It's a great professional opportunity for me and a milestone for the company, but it's just been so long.
W: Yeah. Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough. Nevertheless, I think that with a bit of luck, we'll be done by next week.
M: Ha, you must be delusional.
W: You don't think so?
M: No chance. Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework. Then we need to proofread the whole thing and make sure all selling points are watertight.
W: But that will all take no more than a couple of days.
M: I wasn't finished. When we are done with it and send it upstairs, what do you think will happen?
W: What?
M: They'll argue about it for like a month. There's always going to be the odd board member who intervenes and demands rectifications be made. They might think they're being helpful, but in reality they're being obstructive and hampering progress.
W: Oh, Jeff, you're too preoccupied and cynical. It won't be anywhere as bad as that. You'll see, the entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible, and the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support. Go on then, let's stop there and meet up again same time tomorrow.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material: One thing I've learned in a quarter-century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior, and that there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes. When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe. One such circumstance always comes back to me. It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution. Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth. We reached the deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, "Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for. He used to say, 'When in doubt, assume positive intent.'" And just like that, we had a path forward. My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter; quite likely there were elements of truth in both employees' stories. We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further. We assumed the best about both of them and moved on. The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us. In fact, their problems didn't recur. Over the years, this general approach has proved useful. Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for. For others, it's just a daily occurrence. And that second group of people is becoming the majority as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining. In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking. The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook and 35% reported mixed feelings. When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it and 45% had mixed feelings. Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing. As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing. Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby. Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion. Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out. However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash. Take buying lunch on workdays for example. People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch. Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less. One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home. Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry. It's likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing — and of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner. Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons. But the number-one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag, and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing. If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights. If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection but the passengers might miss the flight. Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit. Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination-coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate. Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared "mishandled" by the carrier. Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged. Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours. The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination. If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days. Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse, and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions. It takes about three months to go from "missing in action" to "irretrievably lost". Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage. And make sure your name is on the bag, along with your phone number, so an agent can contact you.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone. And you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself. In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity. There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful. It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions. And it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy. Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
The study included 128 mostly female student participants. The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation. The conversation couldn't be heard but could be detected through mouth movements. Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participants' conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation. In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone. A third version involved the participants' partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone. If you've experienced a similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions. The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion. They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria. The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation. Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem.
These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion. The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience. This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
More and more people travel for a variety of reasons. Many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business. Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find. After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited, and the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or Bed and Breakfast arrangements. B&Bs, I mean, Bed and Breakfast arrangements are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized, friendly setting. For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles. And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America. The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed. But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business. The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location. If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington, D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B. On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you. Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family. You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the bookkeeping involved. The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income. While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
options: He has distinguished himself in foreign service.
He is his country's ambassador to Winopia.
He is currently an electrical engineer.
He craves attention from the media.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the man from the conversation? 

 【翻译】 从对话中我们了解到这位男士的什么信息? 
 A)  他在外交服务领域表现出色。 
 B)  他是他的国家驻Winopia的大使。 
 C)  他目前是一名电气工程师。 
 D)  他渴望得到媒体的关注。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） He has distinguished himself in foreign service. 
 【定位】 P1 Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats. 
 今天的特邀嘉宾是布莱克韦尔勋爵，他是我国最有经验、最杰出的职业外交官之一。 

 【信号】 主持人开场介绍嘉宾的那一句 。答案信号是"访谈开场主持人对嘉宾的定性介绍"——one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats，访谈类对话里嘉宾身份几乎都在开场这句一锤定音。 

 【替换】 distinguished career diplomats ↔ distinguished himself in foreign service diplomats（外交官）= foreign service（外交事务）的同义改写 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 录音里 Winopia 只是被问及的新闻话题，男方明确说自己 never been involved with Winopian relations（从未涉足对 Winopia 的事务），根本不是该国大使。选项借"Winopia"这个反复出现的地名诱你误选。  借用原文：I've never been involved with Winopian relations 

 C) 原词陷阱 男方说自己 I got a degree in electrical engineering，那只是早年学历，他随后转空军、读法律、入外交界已 22 年。选项用 currently（目前）把旧学历说成现职，是典型"听到 electrical engineer 就想选"的原词陷阱。  借用原文：I got a degree in electrical engineering 

 D) 未提及 通篇是主持人邀他来谈外交，男方对热点新闻还谦称只知道新闻上看到的，没有任何"爱出风头"的迹象。He craves attention from the media. 在录音里毫无依据。

questions.prompt: What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing?
options: A government reshuffle.
A fundamental reform.
Some sort of political reorientation.
Some sort of crisis of legitimacy.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing? 

 【翻译】 这位男士说Winopia政府可能正在经历什么? 
 A)  政府改组。 
 B)  根本性改革。 
 C)  某种政治重新定向。 
 D)  某种合法性危机。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Some sort of crisis of legitimacy. 
 【定位】 P4 It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy, and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on. 
 看起来 Winopia 政府似乎正在经历某种合法性危机，已经过渡性地成立了临时政府，直到选定国家元首为止。 

 【信号】 被问方对局势直接下定性结论的应答 。答案信号是"被问者的直接应答"：主持人问 Winopia 现状，男方应答里直接给出定性 undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy，对话题答案就落在这种"针对提问的正面回答"里。 

 【替换】 some sort of crisis of legitimacy ↔ Some sort of crisis of legitimacy 答案句与选项几乎原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A government reshuffle 指内阁人事调整，远轻于录音所述的 crisis of legitimacy。录音根本没提改组，是用一个程度更轻的政治术语来稀释正解。 
 B) 未提及 A fundamental reform"根本性改革"带积极色彩，而录音说的是危机加临时政府的被动局面，色彩相反且录音从未提"改革"。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Some sort of political reorientation 故意复制录音的 some sort of 句式来制造耳熟，但录音里 some sort of 后接的是 crisis of legitimacy，不是 political reorientation。盗的是句式不是内容。  借用原文：undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy

questions.prompt: According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations?
options: All diplomats have more or less similar stories to tell.
It is a prerequisite to get some practice in diplomacy.
Different people can take different paths.
It is a must to first obtain a law degree.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations? 

 【翻译】 根据这位男士的说法,如何获得外交关系方面的职业? 
 A)  所有外交官都有或多或少相似的故事可讲。 
 B)  获得一些外交实践经验是先决条件。 
 C)  不同的人可以走不同的道路。 
 D)  首先必须获得法律学位。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Different people can take different paths. 
 【定位】 P8 There are many different paths one can take. All diplomats have their own story. 
 可以走的路有很多条。每个外交官都有自己的故事。 

 【信号】 应答开头的总括句，先于个人举例 。答案信号是"被问方应答的第一句总括"——There are many different paths one can take。它出现在男方随后讲自己经历（电气—空军—法律）之前，总括句先于例子，正是答案所在；后面的个人路径只是举例佐证。 

 【替换】 There are many different paths one can take ↔ Different people can take different paths many different paths = different people take different paths，多样性同义 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音 All diplomats have their own story 强调"各有各的"，选项 All diplomats have more or less similar stories to tell 借 All diplomats…story 的外壳，把 own（各自的）偷换成 similar（相似的），意思正好反了。  借用原文：All diplomats have their own story 

 B) 与原文相反 It is a prerequisite to get some practice in diplomacy. 把"实习"说成 prerequisite（必要前提），但男方主张路径多样、从未说存在任何"必备前提"，绝对化表述与"因人而异"相悖。 
 D) 原词陷阱 男方确实提到自己 obtaining a degree in international law，那只是他个人路径的一环。选项 It is a must to first obtain a law degree. 把个人经历拔高成对所有人的"必须"，是听到 law degree 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：upon obtaining a degree in international law

questions.prompt: What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation?
options: Key skills required of a diplomat.
The making of an expert diplomat.
Diplomatic discourse and rhetoric.
Contributions by diplomatic envoys.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation? 

 【翻译】 在对话结束时,说话者主要讨论了什么? 
 A)  外交官所需的关键技能。 
 B)  如何成为一名专业外交官。 
 C)  外交话语和修辞。 
 D)  外交使节的贡献。 

 【答案】 A （主旨题） Key skills required of a diplomat. 
 【定位】 P9 W: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job? M: There are so many. Being a hard worker and a good student is important... a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric...people and communication skills are vital. 
 女：你认为这份工作需要哪些关键技能？男：太多了。做个勤奋的人、好学的人很重要……外交官在言辞和修辞上要非常善于表达……为人处世和沟通能力至关重要。 

 【信号】 结尾一问一答围着"关键技能"展开 。答案信号是"结尾这轮问答的共同焦点"：主持人问 the key skills one needs for the job，男方随后整段都在列举各种 skills，问与答合起来锁定主话题。主旨题靠这种"问答合判"，不靠单句。 

 【替换】 the key skills one needs for the job ↔ Key skills required of a diplomat key skills…for the job = Key skills required of a diplomat，几乎逐词对应 

 【排除】 B) 过度推断 The making of an expert diplomat 谈的是"怎样成长为专家"的全过程，而结尾只在列举工作所需技能，没讲成长路径。它把话题撑得比实际更大。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音确说 articulate in their discourse and rhetoric，但那只是男方列举的众多技能中的一项，Diplomatic discourse and rhetoric 拿一个细节当整段主题，以偏概全。  借用原文：very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric 

 D) 未提及 结尾谈的是技能，没有讨论外交官做出了什么贡献。Contributions by diplomatic envoys. 在结尾内容里没有依据（envoys 一词虽前文出现过，但话题不是贡献）。  借用原文：our expert envoys at our consulate

questions.prompt: Why does the man suggest they call it a day?
options: They have got their work done.
They both look tired
They can meet again tomorrow anyway.
They are both anxious to go home.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the man suggest they call it a day? 

 【翻译】 男士为什么建议他们今天就到此为止? 
 A)  他们已经完成了工作。 
 B)  他们两人看起来都很累。 
 C)  反正他们明天还能再见面。 
 D)  他们都急着想回家。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They both look tired 
 【定位】 P1 It's getting late and we're both displaying signs of weariness. I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning. 
 已经很晚了，我俩都显出疲态了。我觉得今天就到这儿吧，明天上午再继续。 

 【信号】 提议收工那句里紧贴的理由状语 。男方说 I think we should call it a day（提议收工）之前紧跟着 we're both displaying signs of weariness（我俩都显出疲态），这个与提议直接相连的状态描述就是收工理由，是答案信号。 

 【替换】 we're both displaying signs of weariness ↔ They both look tired weariness 改写成 tired，displaying signs 改写成 look 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They have got their work done. 借了原文反复出现的 done（如 we are almost done、we will be all done）来诱选，但那些 done 都带 almost / will be，是『快完了 / 将会完成』，并非已经干完；男方收工理由是累，不是完工。  借用原文：Don't you think we are almost done? 

 C) 答非所问 They can meet again tomorrow anyway. 取自男方 meet again tomorrow morning，但那是收工之后的安排，不是他『为什么要收工』的理由，与 Why 的问法错位。  借用原文：meet again tomorrow morning 

 D) 未提及 They are both anxious to go home. 里 anxious to go home（急切回家）原文没有对应表述；男方只说 call it a day（今天到此），是因为累，并未表现出急切回家的情绪。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say is a little tough?
options: The board members' insufficient support.
Two months devoted to the same contract.
Working two months without any progress.
The man's long concentration on the project.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say is a little tough? 

 【翻译】 女士说什么有点难? 
 A)  董事会成员的支持不足。 
 B)  两个月都投入在同一份合同上。 
 C)  工作两个月却没有任何进展。 
 D)  男士长时间专注于这个项目。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Two months devoted to the same contract. 
 【定位】 P6 Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough. 
 整整两个月只扑在同一份合同上，是有点难熬。 

 【信号】 题干同词 tough 在原文的复现处即落点 。女方原话 Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough 里出现了与题干完全一样的 a little tough，这个评价词所修饰的主语就是答案句的核心。 

 【替换】 Two months working on nothing but the same contract ↔ Two months devoted to the same contract. working on nothing but 改写成 devoted to 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 The board members' insufficient support. 里 board members 确在录音出现，但谈董事会的是男方在 P13 段的牢骚，且女方在 the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support 反而说董事会几乎一致支持；把这话安到女方说 tough 头上，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：demands rectifications be made 

 C) 与原文相反 Working two months without any progress. 多出的 without any progress 与原文相反：女方明说 I think we are making good progress（进展不错），可见难的是『两个月只干一件事』的枯燥，而非没进展。B、C 一字之差，差就差在这里。  借用原文：I think we are making good progress 

 D) 张冠李戴 The man's long concentration on the project. 说的是男方对项目投入太久（呼应 it's just been so long），但题目问的是女方说哪件事 tough；把男方的体验安给女方所评价的难事，主体错位。  借用原文：it's just been so long

questions.prompt: What does the man say the woman must be in thinking they'll finish by next week?
options: Unprofessional.
Inspirational.
Exceptional.
Delusional.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say the woman must be in thinking they'll finish by next week? 

 【翻译】 男士说女士认为他们下周能完成是怎样的想法? 
 A)  不专业的。 
 B)  鼓舞人心的。 
 C)  杰出的。 
 D)  妄想的。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） Delusional. 
 【定位】 P7 Ha, you must be delusional. 
 哈，你一定是在痴心妄想吧。 

 【信号】 男方对女方乐观预期的直接回怼 。女方在 we'll be done by next week 表达乐观，男方紧接着 you must be delusional 直接回应——这句被问者 / 回应方给出的评价就是答案信号，语气还带 Ha 的讥讽。 

 【替换】 you must be delusional ↔ Delusional. 原句评价词直接成选项 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 Unprofessional. 与 delusional 同为贬义，易混；但 delusional 指『脱离现实、妄想』，针对的是女方对工期的乐观判断，并非批评她职业水准。色彩对了，落点错了。 
 B) 与原文相反 Inspirational.（鼓舞人心）是褒义，与男方 Ha, you must be delusional 的讥讽否定语气完全相反，听出语气是贬即可排除。  借用原文：Ha, you must be delusional 

 C) 与原文相反 Exceptional.（出色的）同为褒义，男方并未夸女方，而是讥讽她想法不现实，褒贬方向就不对。  借用原文：you must be delusional

questions.prompt: What does the entire managerial hierarchy want to see according to the woman?
options: Fewer rectifications of the contract.
More support from the board members.
The early implementation of the project.
The alignment of all sections of the contract.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the entire managerial hierarchy want to see according to the woman? 

 【翻译】 根据女士所说,整个管理层想要看到什么? 
 A)  减少对合同的修改。 
 B)  得到董事会成员更多的支持。 
 C)  项目的提前实施。 
 D)  合同所有部分的一致。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The early implementation of the project. 
 【定位】 P14 the entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible 
 整个管理层都希望这个项目尽快落地实施。 

 【信号】 愿望词 wants to see 直接领出答案 。女方 the entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible 里 wants to see 与题干 want to see 完全对应，其后内容即所求愿望，是明确的答案信号。 

 【替换】 this project implemented as soon as possible ↔ The early implementation of the project. 动词 implemented + as soon as possible 改写成名词 early implementation 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Fewer rectifications of the contract. 借了男方 demands rectifications be made 里的 rectifications，但那是男方预测董事会会要求修改的牢骚，不是管理层『想看到』的，且主体是男方说的不是女方说的管理层愿望。  借用原文：demands rectifications be made 

 B) 偷换概念 More support from the board members. 盗用 the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support 里的 support，但女方说的是董事会已经几乎一致支持，并非管理层『想要更多支持』，把现状偷换成了诉求。  借用原文：the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support 

 D) 张冠李戴 The alignment of all sections of the contract. 盗用男方 Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework 里的 aligned / sections，那是男方列举的剩余工作，不是女方所说管理层想看到的结果。  借用原文：Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework

questions.prompt: When can it be hard to know whom to believe?
options: When two employees propose contrary solutions to their dispute.
When two employees are directed by their respective manager.
When two people behave in an apparently clashing manner.
When two people tell different stories of the same event.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 When can it be hard to know whom to believe? 

 【翻译】 什么时候很难知道该相信谁？ 
 A)  当两名员工针对他们的争议提出相反的解决方案时。 
 B)  当两名员工分别由各自的经理指导时。 
 C)  当两个人的行为方式明显相互冲突时。 
 D)  当两个人对同一事件讲述不同的故事时。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） When two people tell different stories of the same event. 
 【定位】 P1 When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe. 
 当两个人对同一件事有不同的版本时，就很难知道该相信谁。 

 【信号】 题干原句几乎照搬 。原文 When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe. 与题干用了同一个结尾 hard to know whom to believe，这种题干与原文句尾高度吻合的呼应，就是答案句的定位信号——前半的 When 从句即是要找的情形。 

 【替换】 different versions of the same event ↔ different stories of the same event versions 改写成 stories 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 用了原文出现的 dispute 一词，但把情形偷换成 propose contrary solutions to their dispute（提出相反的解决方案），而原文说的是对同一事件有不同版本，根本没提双方提解决方案，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes 

 B) 未提及 B 说情形是 two employees are directed by their respective manager（两员工被各自经理指派），原文只提到管理者后来介入处理，从未说难辨真假是因为被经理指派，是未提及的捏造。 
 C) 偷换概念 C 把情形说成 behave in an apparently clashing manner（行为上看起来冲突），但原文界定的是对同一事件说法不同，是认知/陈述层面的分歧，不是行为冲突，偷换了情形的性质。  借用原文：different versions of the same event

questions.prompt: What does the speaker definitely recall about the dispute mentioned as an example?
options: How it got resolved.
How it happened.
What it was about.
When it was settled.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker definitely recall about the dispute mentioned as an example? 

 【翻译】 关于作为例子提到的那次争议,说话者明确记得什么？ 
 A)  它是如何得到解决的。 
 B)  它是如何发生的。 
 C)  它是关于什么的。 
 D)  它是何时解决的。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） How it got resolved. 
 【定位】 P1 It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution. 
 那是多年前的事了，这场冲突有多无足轻重可见一斑——我甚至已不记得争执的内容是什么，但我清楚地记得它是怎么解决的。 

 【信号】 but 转折后才是落点 。句中 I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution 用 but 把前半的不记得内容和后半的记得解决方式分隔开，转折后的 definitely recall the resolution 才是说话人真正强调、也是题干 definitely recall 所问的落点。 

 【替换】 I definitely recall the resolution ↔ How it got resolved 名词 resolution 化为问句方式 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 用了原文出现的 happened（It happened years ago），但那只是交代时间久远，说话人记得的是解决方式不是经过；听到 happened 就选 B 正中圈套。  借用原文：It happened years ago 

 C) 与原文相反 C 问 What it was about（关于什么），但原文恰恰说 I no longer even recall what the dispute was about——这正是说话人不记得的那一面，与题干 definitely recall 正好相反。  借用原文：I no longer even recall what the dispute was about 

 D) 偷换概念 D 问 When it was settled（何时解决），与 A 都涉及解决，但原文记得的是 the resolution（怎么解决）而非解决的时间点，原文只用 years ago 泛指年代，并未交代具体何时 settled，属把方式偷换成时间。

questions.prompt: What did the speaker and his counterpart do when the two employees gave different accounts of the same event?
options: They intervened promptly lest their dispute escalate.
They tried to ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
They assumed the best about them and moved on.
They persuaded them to put their conflict aside.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the speaker and his counterpart do when the two employees gave different accounts of the same event? 

 【翻译】 当两名员工对同一事件给出不同说法时,说话者和他的对应方做了什么？ 
 A)  他们迅速介入,以免争议升级。 
 B)  他们试图查明事情的实际真相。 
 C)  他们对他们做了最好的假设并继续前行。 
 D)  他们说服他们将冲突放在一边。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They assumed the best about them and moved on. 
 【定位】 P1 We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further. We assumed the best about both of them and moved on. 
 我们商定今后留意他们的言行和关系，但不再进一步介入。我们对两人都往好处想，然后向前看了。 

 【信号】 结论句直陈所做 。原文 We assumed the best about both of them and moved on 是对他们行动的直接陈述句，紧接在 to intervene no further 之后收束整段处理过程，是叙述实际所做的结论落点。 

 【替换】 We assumed the best about both of them and moved on ↔ They assumed the best about them and moved on 几乎原句保留只换主语 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 说他们 intervened promptly lest their dispute escalate（及时介入防升级），但原文明说 to intervene no further——决定不再介入，A 的方向与原文正好相反。  借用原文：to intervene no further 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 用了原文原话 ascertain the actual facts of the matter，但原文是 we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter——他们认定查不出真相、放弃了查，B 把这句截头去尾说成他们努力查清，恰好弄反。  借用原文：we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter 

 D) 未提及 D 说他们 persuaded them to put their conflict aside（劝员工搁置冲突），但原文是两位管理者自己决定 moved on，并未去劝说员工放下，是未提及的动作；原文只说 put the conflict behind us，主语是管理者而非劝员工。  借用原文：we were able to put the conflict behind us

questions.prompt: What do an increasing number of Americans do according to the passage?
options: Dine out daily.
Budget sensibly.
Enjoy cooking.
Shop at groceries.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do an increasing number of Americans do according to the passage? 

 【翻译】 根据文章，越来越多的美国人在做什么? 
 A)  每天外出就餐。 
 B)  理性预算。 
 C)  享受烹饪。 
 D)  在杂货店购物。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Dine out daily. 
 【定位】 P1 For others, it's just a daily occurrence. And that second group of people is becoming the majority as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining. 
 对另一些人来说，外出吃饭只是每天都在发生的平常事。而随着喜欢做饭的美国人数量在下降，这第二类人正在成为多数。 

 【信号】 becoming the majority锁定增多的群体 。答案信号是 becoming the majority（正在成为多数），它紧接 that second group of people；而"第二类人"指的正是前一句的 it's just a daily occurrence，即每天外出就餐的人。"成为多数"就是"越来越多"的信号落点。 

 【替换】 it's just a daily occurrence ↔ Dine out daily. 外出就餐+每天的同义改写 
 that second group of people is becoming the majority ↔ Dine out daily. 成为多数对应"越来越多人做" 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 原文开头说第一类人把外食当作 planned and budgeted for 的款待，选项 Budget sensibly. 盗用了 budget 一词，但"做预算"是第一类（少数人）的做法，不是题干问的"越来越多的人"，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：planned and budgeted for 

 C) 与原文相反 选项 Enjoy cooking. 抓住了原文的 cooking 和 enjoy，但原文是 the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining——喜欢做饭的人在"减少"，正与题干"increasing"相反，方向反了。  借用原文：the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 Shop at groceries. 的 grocery 一词原文后段确实出现于 challenges for the grocery industry，但那是讲对杂货业的挑战，不是说"越来越多人去杂货店买菜"，原文从未把"逛杂货店"列为增多的行为，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：challenges for the grocery industry

questions.prompt: What does Eddie Yoon think cooking is akin to?
options: Shopping.
Sewing.
Entertaining oneself.
Fashion designing.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does Eddie Yoon think cooking is akin to? 

 【翻译】 Eddie Yoon认为烹饪类似于什么? 
 A)  购物。 
 B)  缝纫。 
 C)  自我娱乐。 
 D)  时装设计。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Sewing. 
 【定位】 P1 Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing. As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing. 
 尤恩断言，做饭好比缝纫。就在不久前的20世纪初，很多美国人还自己缝制衣服。 

 【信号】 akin to后面紧接的名词 。答案信号就是类比词 akin to，它在原文里直接说出 cooking is akin to sewing，紧跟其后的 sewing 即被类比的对象，定位干净利落。 

 【替换】 cooking is akin to sewing ↔ Sewing. 原词直接对应 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 选项 Shopping. 与原文谈的"买衣服"概念沾边（buy clothing），但原文把做饭类比的是"缝纫"这一动作，从未说做饭类似"购物"，属未提及的张冠李戴。 
 C) 张冠李戴 选项 Entertaining oneself.（自娱自乐）与原文 they do it mainly as a hobby 里的 hobby 略有联想，但 hobby 是说"今天少数人把缝纫当爱好"，并非把做饭类比成"娱乐"，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：they do it mainly as a hobby 

 D) 偷换概念 选项 Fashion designing.（服装设计）与原文反复出现的 clothing / sewed their own clothing 同属"衣服"话题，最易因联想而误选，但原文类比的是"缝纫"这个动作本身，不是"服装设计"，是话题相近的偷换。  借用原文：many Americans sewed their own clothing

questions.prompt: What will Americans be able to do by making their own lunch?
options: Satisfy their taste.
Cut down expenses.
Eat more healthily.
Cultivate new hobbies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What will Americans be able to do by making their own lunch? 

 【翻译】 美国人通过自己做午餐能够做到什么? 
 A)  满足他们的口味。 
 B)  减少开支。 
 C)  吃得更健康。 
 D)  培养新爱好。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Cut down expenses. 
 【定位】 P1 People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch. Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less. One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home. 
 人们买午餐平均每顿花10美元。而自己做午餐则会更便宜。一项调查发现，自带在家做好的午餐时，人们平均只花6.30美元。 

 【信号】 cost less加$10对$6.30的数字对比 。答案信号有两层：一是明示的 Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less（更便宜），二是 \$10 per meal 与 \$6.30 的数字对比，二者都直指"省钱"，是篇章里典型的"对比+数字"答案信号。 

 【替换】 Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less ↔ Cut down expenses. cost less与cut down expenses同义 
 they bring lunch prepared at home ↔ Cut down expenses. 数字证实自己做更省 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 选项 Satisfy their taste.（满足口味）听上去是自己做饭的常见好处，但原文这段只谈钱（cost less、\$6.30），完全没提味道好不好，属未提及。 
 C) 未提及 选项 Eat more healthily.（吃得更健康）是"自己做饭"最容易让人联想到的好处，迷惑性强，但原文论证的全是花钱多少，没有任何关于"健康/营养"的表述，属未提及。 
 D) 张冠李戴 选项 Cultivate new hobbies.（培养新爱好）里的 hobby 概念来自前文讲缝纫的 they do it mainly as a hobby，与"自己做午餐"这一段无关，是把别处的 hobby 嫁接过来，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：they do it mainly as a hobby

questions.prompt: What does the passage say signifies a host of challenges for America's grocery industry?
options: People's intense focus on convenience.
People's deteriorating family finances.
People's strong aversion to junk foods.
People's increasing dislike of cooking.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say signifies a host of challenges for America's grocery industry? 

 【翻译】 文章说什么标志着美国杂货业面临诸多挑战? 
 A)  人们对便利性的强烈关注。 
 B)  人们不断恶化的家庭财务状况。 
 C)  人们对垃圾食品的强烈厌恶。 
 D)  人们对烹饪日益增长的厌恶。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） People's increasing dislike of cooking. 
 【定位】 P1 Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry. 
 美国人越来越不愿在厨房里花时间，这预示着杂货业将面临一系列挑战。 

 【信号】 signifies连接现象与挑战 。答案信号是因果动词 signifies a host of challenges，它把后果"诸多挑战"与紧挨在它前面的现象 Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen 直接绑在一起，前因后果一句话讲完。 

 【替换】 Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen ↔ People's increasing dislike of cooking. 厌恶下厨=越来越不爱做饭的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 People's intense focus on convenience. 借用了原文 what people save in convenience 的 convenience，但原文 convenience 是讲"省下的便利"，并非"对便利的强烈追求带来挑战"，signifies 前挂的现象不是它，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：what people save in convenience, they lose in cash 

 B) 张冠李戴 选项 People's deteriorating family finances. 里的 family finances 来自原文最后一句 detrimentally impact family finances，但那是说"不爱下厨"也会"损害家庭财务"——家庭财务是被影响的后果之一，不是给杂货业带来挑战的原因，张冠李戴。  借用原文：detrimentally impact family finances 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 People's strong aversion to junk foods. 盗用了原文 growing aversion 的 aversion 一词，但原文 aversion 的对象是"在厨房花时间"，不是"垃圾食品"，原文通篇未提 junk food，属原词陷阱叠加无中生有。  借用原文：growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen

questions.prompt: What is the number-one reason a bag ends up lost according to this talk?
options: Its owner's flight is delayed because of bad weather.
Airlines cannot find its owner without an ID tag on it.
Airline staff have not correctly coded its destination tag.
Its owner has forgot to pick it up from the baggage claim.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the number-one reason a bag ends up lost according to this talk? 

 【翻译】 根据这段话，行李箱最终丢失的首要原因是什么? 
 A)  其主人的航班因恶劣天气而延误。 
 B)  航空公司因行李箱上没有身份标签而无法找到其主人。 
 C)  航空公司工作人员没有正确编码其目的地标签。 
 D)  其主人忘记从行李提取处取走它。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Airlines cannot find its owner without an ID tag on it. 
 【定位】 P1 But the number-one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag, and airlines don't know to whom it belongs. 
 但行李丢失的头号原因是它没有身份标签，于是航空公司不知道它属于谁。 

 【信号】 转折词 But 加最高级 number-one 双重锁定 。前文用 Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags and some people simply forgetting to pick up 一口气列了一堆原因(都是干扰)，紧接着用 But the number-one reason 转折并加最高级，这句才是真正要答的"首要原因"。转折 But + 最高级 number-one 是双重答案信号。 

 【替换】 it has no ID tag ↔ without an ID tag on it has no = without 否定同义改写 
 airlines don't know to whom it belongs ↔ Airlines cannot find its owner 不知属于谁=找不到主人 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项的 flight is delayed because of bad weather 直接盗用了录音 Bad weather and flight delays 的原词，但这只是 But 之前罗列的众多次要原因之一，不是 number-one，听到 bad weather 就选正中陷阱。  借用原文：Bad weather and flight delays 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 项 correctly coded its destination tag 对应录音里的 miscoded destination tags，原词照搬，但它同样属于 But 之前的次要原因罗列，并非 number-one，是和 A 同类的原词陷阱。  借用原文：miscoded destination tags 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 forgot to pick it up from the baggage claim 来自录音 some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags，又是罗列区原词，属次要原因，不符合 number-one，依旧是原词陷阱。  借用原文：some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags

questions.prompt: What may happen to your baggage even when there are sophisticated automated systems?
options: Its tag may get torn off on the conveyor belt.
Its tag may get stuck in the sorting machine.
It may be sent to a wrong destination.
It may be picked up by someone else.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What may happen to your baggage even when there are sophisticated automated systems? 

 【翻译】 即使有先进的自动化系统,您的行李可能会发生什么情况? 
 A)  其标签可能在传送带上被撕掉。 
 B)  其标签可能卡在分拣机里。 
 C)  它可能被送到错误的目的地。 
 D)  它可能被其他人取走。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Its tag may get torn off on the conveyor belt. 
 【定位】 P2 Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name. 
 即便如此，所有这些技术也未必能让你的行李标签免于在传送带上被扯掉，结果你成了一个没有名字的行李的主人。 

 【信号】 让步转折 Even so 引出真正后果 。前文 Some airports have sophisticated automated systems 大谈各种先进系统(对应题干 sophisticated automated systems)，随后 Even so 让步转折，点出"技术也救不了标签被扯掉"——Even so 之后才是答案。 

 【替换】 your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt ↔ Its tag may get torn off on the conveyor belt 几乎原句对应稍作改写 
 may not save your baggage tag ↔ Its tag may get torn off 未能保住=可能被扯掉 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 项 stuck in the sorting machine 盗用了录音 sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate 里的 sorting machine 一词，但录音说分拣机是"把行李送到正确登机口"，根本没说标签会卡在里面，属答非所问的原词陷阱。  借用原文：sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate 

 C) 张冠李戴 C 项 sent to a wrong destination 让人联想到第一段 miscoded destination tags，但那是讲"丢失原因"、且不在 Even so 转折后；本题问的是即便技术先进仍会发生的事，录音对应的是标签被扯掉，不是送错地，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：miscoded destination tags 

 D) 未提及 D 项 picked up by someone else 在第二段 Even so 这句里根本没出现，录音说的是标签被扯掉、行李变得无名，没说被别人取走，属未提及。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?
options: Purchase irretrievably lost things at auction.
Contact the airport staff to find our missing bag.
Get the airline agent's phone number before boarding.
Avoid packing valuable items in our checked baggage.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk? 

 【翻译】 讲话者在结尾处建议我们做什么? 
 A)  在拍卖会上购买无法找回的丢失物品。 
 B)  联系机场工作人员寻找我们丢失的行李。 
 C)  登机前获取航空公司代理人的电话号码。 
 D)  避免在托运行李中打包贵重物品。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Avoid packing valuable items in our checked baggage. 
 【定位】 P5 So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage. 
 所以，千万不要把任何真正贵重的东西放进你的托运行李里。 

 【信号】 结尾祈使句 never 直发忠告 。末段以 So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage 起头，So 表收束、never 领出强忠告，正是题干 at the end 的建议落点；这种结尾祈使句就是答案信号。 

 【替换】 never pack anything of real value ↔ Avoid packing valuable items never=Avoid 否定建议同义改写 
 anything of real value ↔ valuable items of real value = valuable 名形互换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项 Purchase irretrievably lost things at auction 盗用了第四段 sold at auction 与 irretrievably lost 的原词，但那是在讲无主行李最终的处置去向，不是讲者给"我们"的忠告，属答非所问的原词陷阱。  借用原文：sold at auction 

 B) 与原文相反 B 项 Contact the airport staff to find our missing bag 与结尾 so an agent can contact you 方向相反：录音说"留下电话以便客服能联系你"，B 却说"我们去联系工作人员找包"，主被动颠倒，属与原文相反/张冠李戴。  借用原文：so an agent can contact you 

 C) 偷换概念 C 项 Get the airline agent's phone number before boarding 盗用了结尾 along with your phone number 的 phone number，但录音说的是"把你自己的电话写在行李上"，不是"登机前去拿客服电话"，偷换了 phone number 的归属与做法，属偷换概念的原词陷阱。  借用原文：along with your phone number

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about using one's smartphone during a face-to-face conversation?
options: It can be behaviorally hazardous.
It can be especially disappointing.
It can be socially harmful.
It can be really embarrassing.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about using one's smartphone during a face-to-face conversation? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于在面对面交谈时使用智能手机说了什么? 
 A)  这在行为上可能是有害的。 
 B)  这可能特别令人失望。 
 C)  这在社交上可能是有害的。 
 D)  这可能真的很令人尴尬。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It can be socially harmful. 
 【定位】 P1 There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful. 
 也有证据表明，这种行为对社交是有害的。 

 【信号】 提示证据的 evidence that 之后即结论 。There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful. 用 evidence that 引出对该行为的正式定性，这类'有证据表明…'结构后面紧跟的就是说话人要立的判断，是答案句信号。 

 【替换】 this behavior is socially harmful ↔ It can be socially harmful. 几乎原句，只把 behavior 换成 It 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 It can be behaviorally hazardous. 借录音反复出现的 behavior 一词（如 this behavior）造误导，但录音说的是'对社交有害'，并未说该行为本身'危险'，属偷换概念。  借用原文：this behavior is socially harmful 

 B) 答非所问 It can be especially disappointing. 像是从 less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions 联想出的'失望'，但录音把它定性为 socially harmful，'让人不太满意'只是表现之一，不是本题要的总定性。  借用原文：less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions 

 D) 未提及 It can be really embarrassing. 的'尴尬'在录音里完全没有出现，是凭'玩手机让人尴尬'的生活常识硬补的，属未提及。

questions.prompt: How did the participants in the new study respond regarding phone use during social interactions?
options: They considered it inevitable.
They held a negative view towards it.
They were concerned with its effects.
They saw it as a sign of social evolution.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did the participants in the new study respond regarding phone use during social interactions? 

 【翻译】 新研究中的参与者对社交互动期间使用手机是如何回应的? 
 A)  他们认为这是不可避免的。 
 B)  他们对此持负面看法。 
 C)  他们担心其影响。 
 D)  他们将其视为社会进化的标志。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） They held a negative view towards it. 
 【定位】 P4 The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions. 
 参与者对社交互动中使用手机持负面看法。 

 【信号】 主体 participants + 态度词 negative view 。The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions. 在题干主体 participants 出场处直接给出态度词 negative view，主体与评价词同现，是态度题的答案句信号。 

 【替换】 The participants had a negative view ↔ They held a negative view towards it 近乎原句，had→held、of→towards、加代词 They/it 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 They considered it inevitable. 说参与者认为玩手机'不可避免'，录音只说他们持负面看法，从未谈'是否不可避免'，属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 They were concerned with its effects. 借录音里反复出现的 effects（如 adverse effects）造干扰，但那是研究者发现的客观影响，本题问的是参与者的态度，参与者是'持负面看法'而非'担忧其影响'。  借用原文：adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging 

 D) 与原文相反 They saw it as a sign of social evolution. 把玩手机说成'社会进化的标志'（正面），与录音 negative view 极性完全相反，属与原文相反。  借用原文：The participants had a negative view

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say can result from the common behavior of using phones during face-to-face conversations?
options: Elaborate forms of social contact.
Ill effects on one's sense of pride.
Poor relationships with others.
Vicious cycles of detachment.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say can result from the common behavior of using phones during face-to-face conversations? 

 【翻译】 说话者说在面对面交谈时使用手机这种常见行为会导致什么? 
 A)  复杂形式的社交接触。 
 B)  对个人自尊感的不良影响。 
 C)  与他人的不良关系。 
 D)  疏离的恶性循环。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Vicious cycles of detachment. 
 【定位】 P6 This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others. 
 即便我们试图与他人建立联系，这种常见行为也会造成疏离的恶性循环。 

 【信号】 篇末 can create 引出最终后果 。This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment 出现在全篇最后一句，用 can create 直接引出该行为的最终后果，是篇末收束式答案句信号。 

 【替换】 vicious cycles of detachment ↔ Vicious cycles of detachment. 原词短语整体复现，仅首字母大写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Elaborate forms of social contact. 借录音 they elaborate our understanding 里的 elaborate 造干扰，但那里 elaborate 是动词'使更丰富（我们的理解）'，与'精致的社交形式'毫无关系，且方向上录音讲的是坏后果，A 听着像好事。  借用原文：they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect 

 B) 答非所问 Ill effects on one's sense of pride. 借 self-esteem（自尊）改写成 pride，录音确实说过对自尊有不良影响，但那是中段提到的影响，本题问 result from 的最终后果（末句的 vicious cycles），B 答非所问。  借用原文：adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem 

 C) 答非所问 Poor relationships with others. 像是从 the quality of the relationship 来的'人际变差'，意思虽与 D 相近，但本题答案信号句末句用的是 vicious cycles of detachment，C 既非该后果句的措辞、又是参与者对关系质量的评判而非最终后果，故不选。  借用原文：the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say travelers commonly complain about?
options: The ill treatment they get as tourists.
The nonprofessional business they see.
The impersonal accommodations.
The many adventures on their way.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say travelers commonly complain about? 

 【翻译】 说话者说旅行者通常抱怨什么？ 
 A)  他们作为游客受到的不良待遇。 
 B)  他们看到的不专业的商业行为。 
 C)  缺乏人情味的住宿条件。 
 D)  旅途中的诸多冒险经历。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The impersonal accommodations. 
 【定位】 P1 Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find. 
 无论出行的理由是什么，旅行者们一个共同的抱怨就是他们遇到的那种缺乏人情味的住宿。 

 【信号】 complaint 信号词直接引出 。答案句里 a common complaint of travelers is 与题干 commonly complain about 的抱怨信号严丝合缝，complaint 之后紧跟的 the impersonal accommodations 就是抱怨的对象，是典型的信号词后面接答案。 

 【替换】 a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations ↔ The impersonal accommodations. 近乎原句压缩 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 The ill treatment they get as tourists. 把抱怨说成受差待遇，但原文从头到尾说的是住宿缺人情味、千篇一律，并没提任何被恶待、被歧视的内容，属于无中生有的升级。 
 B) 原词陷阱 The nonprofessional business they see. 借用了原文 personal or professional business 里的 professional 一词，但原文那句是说人们因私事或公务出行，根本没说他们抱怨不专业的生意，是听到 professional 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：many venture forth on personal or professional business 

 D) 与原文相反 The many adventures on their way. 说一路有许多奇遇，是正面体验，而题目问的是抱怨（负面）；原文也无奇遇之说，方向与抱怨正相反，自然不选。

questions.prompt: What is said about Bed and Breakfast arrangements?
options: They have been the classic way to visit Europe.
They attract tourists with location and decoration.
They have long been competing with chain hotels.
They are in fact a completely new idea in America.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is said about Bed and Breakfast arrangements? 

 【翻译】 关于家庭旅馆安排说了什么？ 
 A)  它们一直是游览欧洲的经典方式。 
 B)  它们以地理位置和装饰吸引游客。 
 C)  它们长期以来一直在与连锁酒店竞争。 
 D)  它们实际上在美国是一个全新的概念。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They have been the classic way to visit Europe. 
 【定位】 P2 For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles. And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America. 
 几十年来，B&B 一直是游览欧洲、尤其是不列颠群岛的经典方式。而且事实上，它们在美国也并非真正的新事物。 

 【信号】 For decades 强调由来已久 。For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe 用 For decades（几十年来）加现在完成时强调长期如此，与下一句 not really a new idea 一正一补都在说它由来已久、不是新事物，时间状语就是这里的答案信号。 

 【替换】 B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe ↔ They have been the classic way to visit Europe. 几乎原句搬运 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 They attract tourists with location and decoration. 说靠地段和装潢吸引游客，location 一词确在原文第三段 not only the building itself, but the location 出现过，但那是讲房主开店要考虑的因素，不是说 B&B 整体靠地段装潢揽客，把后文的考量错安成对 B&B 的定性。  借用原文：not only the building itself, but the location 

 C) 未提及 They have long been competing with chain hotels. 提到与连锁酒店长期竞争，但原文只说 B&B 提供个性化、友好的住宿来对抗千篇一律的感觉，从未提到 chain hotels 或彼此竞争，属凭常识脑补出的内容。 
 D) 与原文相反 They are in fact a completely new idea in America. 说在美国是全新事物，恰与原文 they are not really a new idea in America 相反——原文明确用 not 否定了新事物，选项却去掉否定取了反义，是漏听否定词导致的正话反说。  借用原文：they are not really a new idea in America

questions.prompt: What is the first thing you have to consider if you want to start a B&B business?
options: Your financial status.
Your family's consent.
Your property.
Your personality.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the first thing you have to consider if you want to start a B&B business? 

 【翻译】 如果你想开办家庭旅馆生意，你首先必须考虑什么？ 
 A)  你的财务状况。 
 B)  你家人的同意。 
 C)  你的房产。 
 D)  你的个性。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Your property. 
 【定位】 P3 The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location. 
 首先要考虑的是你的房产，不仅是建筑本身，还有它的地理位置。 

 【信号】 The first consideration 排序信号 。The first consideration is your property 用 The first consideration 明示第一项考虑，与题干 the first thing to consider 完全对应，排序信号词直接锁定 property。 

 【替换】 The first consideration is your property ↔ Your property. 原词直接对应 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 Your financial status. 财务状况听上去像开店头等大事，极易凭常识选中，但原文把财务排在 The final consideration is a financial one——是最后一项而非第一项，错在排序。  借用原文：The final consideration is a financial one 

 B) 偷换概念 Your family's consent. 说要家人同意，原文只说要考虑 the lifestyle of you and your family——家人是否真心喜欢接待客人，谈的是生活方式契合度，并非要谁点头同意，是把原文意思偷换成了同意。  借用原文：the lifestyle of you and your family 

 D) 答非所问 Your personality. 性格虽与原文 truly enjoy visitors（是否真心喜欢客人）沾边，但那属于第二项生活方式考量，且原文用的是 lifestyle 而非 personality；它既非第一项、也不是原文对首项的说法。  借用原文：truly enjoy visitors

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say potential B&B hosts must be realistic about?
options: Costs for starting the business.
The number of guests to receive.
The facilities to provide.
Opportunities for income.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say potential B&B hosts must be realistic about? 

 【翻译】 说话者说潜在的家庭旅馆经营者必须对什么有现实认识？ 
 A)  创业的成本。 
 B)  接待客人的数量。 
 C)  提供的设施。 
 D)  收入机会。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Opportunities for income. 
 【定位】 P3 The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income. 
 最后一项考虑是财务方面的，准 B&B 房主必须对赚钱的机会抱有现实的预期。 

 【信号】 realistic about 原词搭桥 。答案句 must be realistic about opportunities for income 与题干 must be realistic about 用词几乎一致，realistic about 后面紧跟的 opportunities for income 就是要现实看待的对象，信号词直接搭桥。 

 【替换】 must be realistic about opportunities for income ↔ Opportunities for income. 原句截取核心宾语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Costs for starting the business. 借了原文 low initial costs 里的 costs，但原文是说启动成本通常很低，并不是说要对成本抱现实预期；要现实看待的明明是收入，这里用真念过的 costs 设了反向陷阱。  借用原文：B&Bs usually have low initial costs 

 B) 答非所问 The number of guests to receive. 说要现实看待接待客人的数量，原文确提到 at least five rooms rented regularly（至少五间房常租出），但那是用来说明靠 B&B 谋生不易的例子，落点仍是收入机会，不是叫房主对客人数量本身抱现实预期。  借用原文：at least five rooms rented regularly 

 C) 张冠李戴 The facilities to provide. 说设施，facilities 一词出现在原文第三段讲房产的部分 facilities for the traveler，那是第一项房产的考量，与本题问的财务上要现实看待什么不在一处，被跨段挪来当答案。  借用原文：facilities for the traveler
